input.quote: Such inspections may be made no more than once each calendar year, at reasonable times and upon reasonable notice. Commerce One shall bear all costs and expenses of such inspection.
input.rationale: Section 4.4 binds Corio (our party) to open its books to inspection at Commerce One's instance. Frequency (once per calendar year), auditor independence (independent CPA reasonably acceptable to Corio), cost allocation (Commerce One bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%) already meet the preferred position, and there is no system-access right. However, notice is only "reasonable notice" rather than 30 days' prior written notice, timing is only "reasonable times" rather than business hours, and the auditor is not expressly bound by confidentiality. Minimal edit adds those three protections plus off-site/no-systems-access wording.

proposal.summary: Add 30 days' written notice, business-hours limitation and confidentiality obligation on the auditor
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added thirty (30) days' prior written notice, confined inspections to our normal business hours, and required the auditor to be bound by confidentiality, consistent with our audit playbook position; the existing annual frequency and Commerce One cost-bearing (subject to the 5% underpayment threshold) are acceptable as drafted.

ops.oldText: Such inspections may be made no more than once each calendar year, at reasonable times and upon reasonable notice.
ops.newText: Such inspections may be made no more than once each calendar year, during Corio's normal business hours and upon at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice, and shall be conducted off-site wherever practicable and without access to Corio's systems or networks. Prior to any such inspection, the accountant shall execute a written confidentiality agreement with Corio no less protective of Corio's Confidential Information than Section 10 of this Agreement.
